title: Brain Collection Schema — v0.1.5
description: Defines all brain collections in brain/machine_artifacts/content/, their record types, and artifact generation rules. All brain content is JSON. Diagrams live in brain/machine_artifacts/diagrams/.

governance.purpose: Corporate policies, AI governance, risk acceptance, safety signoff

architecture.purpose: System and business architecture, component definitions, refactor designs

business_plan.purpose: Business model, investor docs, cost analysis, revenue strategy

sprint_plan.purpose: Sprint planning, backlog, feature requests, UAT feature lists

bugs.purpose: All system bugs. Source of truth for defect tracking. Constrained by CV-008 (bug_type) and CV-009 (bug_resolution_status).

record_schema.title: bugs_schema
record_schema.description: This ChatHealthy Brain Schema documents all bugs in all environments with their statuses. It is an integral part in ChatHealthy's ability to both track bugs and do full or partial regression testing.

req_id.description: Reference to the agile_backlog requirement this bug is associated with (e.g. FC-SELECT-001-REQ-002). Every bug must trace to a requirement.

reason.description: Free text description of the bug

pytest_id.description: Reference to the pytest that validates the fix

pytest_success_criteria.description: Success criteria from the pytest record — mandatory, not freetext

due_date.description: Date bug must be resolved by

success_criteria_to_close.description: What must be true to close this bug

risk_acceptance_id.description: Reference to risk_acceptance.json entry. Null until Boss authorizes. Pydantic object checks this — if not null, fix is authorized. If null, escalate.

ai_operations.purpose: AI model decisions, SIT reports, GPT findings, usage, budget, dead code enforcement
ai_operations.title: ai_operations_schema
ai_operations.description: This ChatHealthy Brain Schema documents AI operational data including model selection decisions, system integration test reports, and dead code enforcement records.

legacy_record.description: Unconstrained legacy records. Will be schema-constrained in a future pass.

dead_code_record.description: A single unreferenced code block found by the v4-031 dead code scanner, marked for deletion.

status.description: commented = Stage 1, deleted = Stage 2, restored = Boss decided to keep

justification.description: Why the scanner flagged this as dead

devops.purpose: Build promotion, deploy config, support tickets

work_log.purpose: Session transcripts, collaboration logs, activity state

prompt_log.purpose: Rolling 24h conversation log — every prompt and response

LogRecords.description: Array of LogRecord objects stored in the utterances field of conversation_log.json.

LogRecord.description: A single utterance in the conversation log. Four types: user (Skip), assistant (Claude), agent (ConversationLogAgent), service (ConversationLogManagerService).

userId.description: Author identifier: Skip, Claude, ConversationLogAgent, or ConversationLogManagerService

timestamp_pst.description: PST time with microsecond precision. Unique across all records (B007).

content.description: Verbatim text content of the utterance

jobId.description: Unique job identifier for agent utterances

errorLogFileId.description: Anthropic Files API file_id for the persistent error log

preservePastTime.description: The PST datetime cutoff used for this job

counts.description: Record counts for the job: original in file, retained for client, archived to MongoDB

action.description: Service action performed (e.g. started, called_agent, wrote_file)

outcome.description: Result of the service action (success, failure)

error.required_when: role in (agent, service) and error occurred
error.description: Error details if the action failed

agile_backlog.purpose: All epics, features, stories, and boolean testable requirements
agile_backlog.title: agile_backlog_schema
agile_backlog.description: This ChatHealthy Brain Schema documents all requirements for ChatHealthy.ai LLC. It is an integral part in ChatHealthy's ability to both track all requirements, map them to the firm's business goals, and facilitate full or partial regression testing.

epic.description: Top-level business component. Contains features[]. Creation requires Boss authority.

epic_id.description: Sequential, assigned by Claude. Never reused. Never user-facing.

name.description: Human-readable business component name (per v4-030). This is what users see.

type.description: operational = user-facing product capability. functional = business function that supports operations.

features.description: Array of features belonging to this epic

feature.description: A capability within an epic. Contains stories[].

feature_id.description: Short uppercase identifier. Convention: abbreviated epic name + capability (e.g. FC-SEARCH, FC-FILT, EVAL-SCORE). Claude assigns.

realized_by.description: Technical components that implement this feature. Free text until architecture component IDs are defined post-alpha. Will reference architecture.json component IDs.

stories.description: Array of stories belonging to this feature

story.description: A unit of deliverable work within a feature. Contains requirements[].

requirements.description: Array of boolean-testable requirements belonging to this story

requirement.description: A boolean-testable assertion. Leaf node of the hierarchy.

pytest_ids.description: References to pytests that validate this requirement. At least one required when implemented.

test_method.description: How this requirement is tested. Determines runner behavior.

test_timeout_seconds.description: Timeout in seconds for test execution. Default 120. Playwright tests should use 180+. DB-heavy tests may need more.

bug_ids.description: Links to bugs filed against this requirement

realized_by.description: Technical components that implement this requirement. Free text until architecture component IDs are defined post-alpha.

depends_on.description: Stories this requirement depends on. If the dependency story fails, this requirement cannot pass.

prompt_log.title: Prompt Log Protocol
prompt_log.description: Operational protocol for how actors write to prompt_log.json. Loaded by the brain boot process.

write_rules: At session start, read prompt_log.json. Determine next utterance number: max(existing utterances) + 1, or 1 if empty.
After every user prompt: append an utterance with role=user and actor identifying who sent it (e.g. Skip).
After every assistant response: append an utterance with role=assistant and actor identifying who responded (e.g. Claude, GPT).
Write each utterance immediately after it occurs. Do not batch.
If the write fails, continue the conversation. Record failure in application log.
content_rules: Text only — never write binary, base64, or images. Replace with [binary content omitted].
Tool results exceeding 500 chars truncated to first 500 chars + [truncated — N chars].
System-reminder content (tags and their contents) excluded from the log.
Credential redaction is NOT handled by prompt_log. See EPIC-4: Security.
grooming_rules: Claude does not groom, renumber, or delete utterances.
Grooming deletes utterances where timestamp_utc < now_utc - 24h.
Grooming does not renumber remaining utterances.
Groom operation must be idempotent: repeated execution produces identical state.
enforcement: Logging is enforced by Claude Code hooks, not by Claude's discipline.
UserPromptSubmit hook fires on every user message and appends to prompt_log.json.
Stop hook fires when Claude finishes responding and appends Claude's response from the transcript.
Hooks are configured in .claude/settings.json and run automatically outside Claude's control.
actor_rules: Actor is an open vocabulary: Skip, Claude, GPT, or any future participant.
New actors are added as they join the discourse. No controlled vocabulary gate.
timestamp_rules: Every utterance has both timestamp_pst and timestamp_utc.
Grooming decisions use timestamp_utc only. timestamp_pst is for display.
